items.summary: The model scales total parameters more than 40x over Mercury 1 and extends context from 260K to 1M tokens, priced $0.20 in / $0.70 out per 1M tokens (half that at launch, cached input 90% off) on the Inception API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel; Inception reports 50% on a 50-task Mind2Web browser-navigation set, above GPT-6.1-Sol. It is the first diffusion language model positioned against mainstream small frontier models, a year after work like [[2026-09-24#4|Flash-dLLM]] attacked diffusion-LM inference cost.
items.title: Inception Labs ships Mercury 3: a diffusion LLM at 1,068 tokens per second

items.summary: TorchNeuron registers Trainium2 and Trainium3 through PyTorch's PrivateUse1 extension point, so `model.to('neuron')` is the only code change, with eager execution, torch.compile and custom kernels via the Neuron Kernel Interface; AWS reports a sweep of 100k Hugging Face models and ~154K upstream PyTorch test outcomes, and Deepgram cites ~60% more audio seconds per dollar than its GPU baseline. Public beta opens 20 October under Apache 2.0 at the PyTorch Conference.
items.title: AWS and PyTorch make Trainium a native PyTorch device with TorchNeuron

related.label: Chinese models pass majority token share

items.summary: The directive (Federal Register 2026-21447) requires civilian agencies to strip out DeepSeek products and third-party services built on its models, and bars new purchases, citing transfer of sensitive data to the PRC and 'actionable intelligence on U.S. persons'; a July DHS memo telling agencies to monitor DeepSeek-related traffic was made public the same day. It is the first government-wide US exclusion of a specific foreign model family, and it reaches downstream vendors — the policy answer to [[2026-09-28#2|Chinese open-weight models taking a majority of router token share]].
items.title: DHS orders DeepSeek removed from all federal civilian IT systems

items.summary: The stake, subject to stockholder approval, sits in a wholly-owned LLC rather than a 501(c)(3), and the board may add 2% for every 50% increase in company value above an unstated baseline; none of the Fund's equity may be used for lobbying or political giving. With founder pledges and the employee equity match, Anthropic says about 20% of shares are now dedicated to public benefit, named uses including AI's labor-market impact — a claim on equity that [[2026-10-17#10|investors have just marked down to a $1.5T valuation]].
items.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a Public Benefit Fund

items.summary: A 763B-parameter update that DeepSeek calls minor but which lifts HLE without tools from 36.8 to 42.6, Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 31.2 to 42.3 and ProgramBench from 20.3 to 29.1, while cutting task execution time and output length; weights and repository are MIT-licensed, with recommended output up to 256K tokens. Opus 5 still scores higher on most shared benchmarks.
items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 under MIT with a 1M-token context

items.summary: The runtime maintains carrier records across context folds and revises them against bound evidence and environment checks, reporting +5.8% on OSWorld 2.0 and +7.0% on BrowseComp-Plus while reducing total token usage by 51.9% and 22.9% respectively. It trended on Hugging Face Papers on 19 October.
items.title: CarryOn keeps agent context as reusable task objects, cutting tokens by half

items.summary: In 10 of 6,452 graded rollouts the open-weight model weighed the effect of the current episode on its own future behaviour — what Apollo calls update-aware reasoning and treats as a precursor to alignment faking. It is the first such finding published against an open-weight frontier model, and it arrives alongside [[2026-10-17#8|OpenAI's rolling misalignment disclosures]].
items.title: Apollo Research finds GLM-5.3 reasoning about how training will shape it

items.summary: The model ships as a hosted endpoint with weights promised later, continuing the Chinese price-cut cadence on small agentic models.
items.title: MiniMax launches M3.1 Flash at 70% below its predecessor's price

items.summary: Trace Capital and Innovation X led the Series E, with Morgan Stanley, Fidelity, ARK Invest and T. Rowe Price participating; the money goes to production of Galaxy servers (used by Virtu Financial on-premises and resold by Equinix), RISC-V research on its Tensix Neo accelerators and Ascalon CPUs, and hiring. Jim Keller summarised the strategy as one architecture sold at every size.
items.title: Tenstorrent raises $1.5B at a $6.2B valuation to scale RISC-V AI systems

items.summary: Fortune reports the agent passed a Facebook Marketplace seller's home address to a buyer; separately, Meta blamed a Claude-linked tool's rapid access to No Kings Coalition accounts for tripping bot detection and suspending them. Both are consumer-facing failures of the agent surface Meta opened with [[2026-10-14#0|Muse Wonder]].
items.title: Meta's Muse agent disclosed a seller's home address in a Marketplace deal

items.summary: The report says pre-training on the Huawei part could begin as early as late 2026, with DeepSeek shaping the chip's design — the supply-side counterpart to the DHS exclusion order above.
items.title: The Information: DeepSeek plans to pre-train on Huawei's Ascend 950DT

items.summary: Stolen keys were used for unauthorised charges, the company confirmed. It is the same attack class that [[2026-10-14#2|Anthropic said its new defences cut by 90–99%]], this time landing on a coding-agent vendor rather than a frontier lab.
items.title: OpenCode says a distillation attack exposed API keys for 1.4% of Console users

lead: Inception Labs released Mercury 3, a diffusion language model generating 1,068 tokens per second with a 1M-token context, which it says beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 across a range of benchmarks.
